stories.head: True Anomaly scores $190M Series C
stories.body: True Anomaly has raised $190 million in a Series C round, valuing the co-orbital security startup at $1.6 billion. This funding underscores the growing demand for space domain awareness solutions as the DoD pushes for enhanced capabilities. The round was led by a mix of existing and new investors, signaling confidence in the startup's trajectory.
stories.soWhat: In a sector where cash is king, True Anomaly's success shows that even in a crowded field, the right narrative can still attract hefty checks.

stories.head: Firefly and SSC Space aim for 2028 launch
stories.body: SSC Space and Firefly have set a target for their first orbital launch from Sweden’s Esrange in 2028. This ambitious timeline indicates a serious commitment to expanding launch capabilities in Europe, as the region seeks to establish itself as a viable alternative to traditional launch markets. The collaboration could also help streamline regulatory challenges in the region.
stories.soWhat: If they hit their timeline, this could shift European launch dynamics, but let’s be honest: in space, timelines are more like suggestions.

stories.head: Orbital plans 100,000 satellites for data centers
stories.body: Startup Orbital has filed with the FCC to deploy up to 100,000 satellites to support burgeoning AI data needs. While the scale is unprecedented, concerns about space debris and orbital congestion are already being raised. The proposal highlights the increasing intersection of AI and space, but at what environmental cost?
stories.soWhat: If we thought the space junk problem was bad now, just wait until we have a hundred thousand more reasons to worry.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser moves forward
watchlist.body: With its DoD variant clearing a critical design review, the next steps will be crucial for Sierra Space as it aims to secure government contracts.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension implications
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480 million extension suggests a long-term commitment to ground station capabilities, which could influence future government tech contracts.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris collaboration
watchlist.body: Their joint bid for a tactical SDA constellation could reshape how military space operations are conducted, especially in contested environments.

watchlist.title: ESA's lunar mapping capability needs
watchlist.body: The European Space Agency's search for lunar mapping data indicates a potential shift in how international collaborations are approached for lunar missions.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
